transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-07
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Gomez (Redwood SE), Tariq Hussain (Redwood), Maya Chen (AuroraPay Head of ML), Raj Singh (CTO), Liam O'Neill (SRE), Priya Reddy (PM)

Summary: quick POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modelling for AuroraPay's fraud-detection + customer messaging scoring flow. Discussed QPS targets, concurrency, token distributions, success criteria, and initial benchmark plan. Agreed next steps to share sample traffic and run 1-week benchmark on dedicated nodes.

Topics: workload sizing, QPS, concurrency, input/output token distribution, latency SLOs, benchmarks, dedicated vs hosted, security (VPC, SOC2, KMS)

[00:00] Samir: hey everybody, thanks for joining, this is Samir from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with me is elena who will lead the bench planning. quick intros?
[00:12] Maya: hi i'm maya, head of ml at aurorapay, we own the scoring pipelines.
[00:16] Raj: raj here, cto, i'll be pulled in for infra and procurement decisions.
[00:20] Liam: liam, platform/sre, will look after network/VPC peering.
[00:24] Priya: priya, product manager for fraud orchestration.
[00:27] Elena: thanks all. quick agenda: understand your traffic patterns (qps & concurrency), token sizes, success criteria for POC, what benchmarks we should run, and timeline.

[02:03] Maya: high level, we do two main calls to the model: a short prompt for intent/classification (like 80-150 tokens in), and a longer rewritting/generation for messaging (typical output 200-500 tokens). Overall mix is roughly 70% classification, 30% generation.

[03:10] Elena: good. can you give ballpark qps and concurrency?
[03:15] Maya: peak QPS for classification about 180 qps, sustained during business hours maybe 90 qps, gen peak around 30 qps. concurrency wise we see bursts up to ~220 concurrent in flight during campaigns. but avg concurrency is lower, maybe 70.

[04:12] Samir: so to summarize — peak combined QPS ~210-220, sustained ~120, concurrency peak ~220, avg ~70. is that fair?
[04:18] Maya: yes, that's accurate.

[05:00] Raj: our success criteria for POC: 1) meet p95 latency under 800ms for classification, p95 under 2s for generation, 2) reduce per-call cost by at least 25% vs our current cloud-hosted pipeline, 3) no data leakage and full audit logs, 4) easy rollout plan into prod.

[06:40] Elena: good, we'll map those to hardware choices. we typically run classification on quantized 4-bit variants with batching and caching, while generation may use fp16 or quantized dequant path depending on quality tradeoffs. for the benchmark we'll run both: a throughput test (sustained qps) and tail latency workloads (spiky concurrency).

[08:25] Liam: network question — during the pilot we want VPC peering and private connectivity, can you support that with dedicated?
[08:33] Samir: yes, dedicated and private both support VPC peering, we'll need IP ranges and firewall rules. for pilot we can do dedicated nodes in our cloud region, and set up peering with a limited set of endpoints.

[09:05] Maya: on tokens: our sample stats show classification requests median input tokens ~110, 90th percentile ~180. outputs for classification are small, median 20 tokens. generation inputs median 150, outputs median 280, 95th around 520 tokens. overall request tokens distribution: median total ~130 tokens, 95th ~480.

[10:52] Elena: excellent, that's concrete. for cost modelling we will use token distribution histograms. can you share anonymized histogram + a CSV of request sizes?
[10:58] Maya: yes will do.

[12:00] Samir: benchmark plan idea: 1) run synthetic replay of 48h traffic at scale to measure throughput and average cost per request; 2) run stress test to emulate campaign bursts (simulate 220 concurrent), measure p50/p95/p99; 3) run quality regression checks on a sample of prompts to ensure quantized models meet accuracy thresholds.

[13:35] Priya: how long does each phase take?
[13:40] Elena: the initial 48h replay + basic metrics should take 3-5 days to run once we have the sample and access. stress tests can run in parallel and take 1-2 days. quality checks depend on eval set size, but plan for 2-3 days. overall pilot 2-3 weeks plus one week for analysis — so 3-4 weeks total.

[15:12] Raj: what hardware do you recommend?
[15:20] Elena: for your mix, a mix of 4x A100 80GB nodes for generation-heavy runs or 8x A100 40GB with GPU packing via batching; we can also test on 8-bit/4-bit quantized model variants on T4/RTX class for classification to reduce cost. we'll propose a config in the benchmark doc.

[16:44] Maya: any known regression risk with 4-bit quant on our prompts? we have some sensitive classification thresholds.
[16:50] Elena: there is always a small delta; that's why we run the quality regression. we typically set a tolerance band (e.g., <2% drop in f1 or precision at target thresholds) as a success criteria. if fails we'll try hybrid: quantized for classification path, fp16 for generation.

[18:10] Samir: what about tooling integration — we need tracing, per-route metrics, and cost breakdowns tied to routes.
[18:18] Elena: Redwood Console provides token-level cost, per-model/per-route latency breakdowns and traces. we can give you dashboard access during pilot and hook in your tracing ID.

[19:30] Liam: security/controls: SOC 2 is fine, but we need KMS key control and audit logs retained for 1 year. can you support customer-managed keys?
[19:40] Samir: yes, private supports customer KMS/HSM integration and we can enable audit log exports to your cloud storage. we'll share the security pack.

[21:05] Maya: curious on multi-region/fallback — campaigns spike across regions, do you support smart routing and fallbacks?
[21:12] Elena: yes, smart routing routes requests by region and can fallback to compatible model variants if capacity constrained. that will be part of our resilience testing.

[22:20] Raj: pricing — how do we estimate per-call cost for mixed workloads?
[22:28] Samir: we model per-token cost + infra amortized across run; for the pilot we'll give you an estimated cost-per-req using your token histograms and our measured throughput. target is to beat your current per-call cost by 25% at parity in accuracy.

[24:00] Priya: ok sample artifacts to share: we'll provide 48h of anonymized request logs (CSV), current latency/cost dashboard screenshots, and the eval prompts set (about 600 examples).

[25:10] Elena: good. benchmarks we'll run:
- Replay at sustained 120 qps and peak 210-220 qps for 48h
- Stress burst test: ramp to 250 concurrency for 5 minutes then back down, repeated to emulate campaigns
- Latency SLO measurement: measure p50/p95/p99 for both classification and generation paths
- Cost run: capture token counts and total infra usage to compute $/request
- Quality regression: run eval set through quantized and fp16 variants and compare metrics

[28:05] Maya: for the replay, do you need full payloads or just token sizes and routes?
[28:12] Elena: best is anonymized prompts + tokenized counts so we can reproduce distribution and run quality checks. full payload only if sanitized.

[30:00] Samir: timeline recap: customer shares data by 2025-08-09, we kickoff benchmark 2025-08-12, run 1 week of active benchmarking (with analysis) and reconvene 2025-08-21 for results and next steps. does that fit?
[30:18] Maya: yes.

[31:00] Raj: procurement questions — will pilot require a commitment?
[31:06] Samir: pilot is billed, short-term commitment for the reserved nodes during the run. we'll include terms in the pilot contract; nothing long-term locked in.

[32:20] Liam: network: we'll confirm IP ranges and peering details by 2025-08-11. also want to validate throughput across peered connection (we have a 10Gbps link).

[33:40] Elena: one more note on modeling: when we compute cost we'll include batching factors — e.g., classification benefits significantly from batching and KV/prefix caching; we'll measure effective tokens-per-second and compute amortized GPU cost.

[35:10] Maya: can you also include a scenario for a hosted fallback (no peering) in case peering isn't ready?
[35:18] Samir: yes, we can run on hosted endpoints with TLS and VPC egress; latency will be slightly higher but it's a viable fallback.

[36:55] Priya: stakeholders: who on your side will present results?
[37:00] Elena: elena and samir will present results, with Tariq for infra notes. we'll prepare a slide summary and raw metric exports.

[38:45] Maya: any specific benchmarks for accuracy vs quantization? we want the test to ensure thresholds around our fraud recall metric.
[38:52] Elena: we'll run the eval set and compute recall/precision; success if recall drop <2% and precision similar. if not, recommend hybrid model.

[40:15] Raj: competitors — we're also talking to openai for hosted endpoints and anthropic for targeted safety, want to see results before deciding.

[41:10] Samir: understood. we'll surface the tradeoffs in the benchmark doc.

[42:00] Elena: deliverables after benchmark: detailed latency & throughput report, cost model mapping token histograms to $/request, quality regression report, and recommended deployment config (nodes, model variant, fallback).

[44:05] Maya: operational question: what SLAs can you offer post-pilot?
[44:12] Samir: for Dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets per contract — we'll discuss depending on committed capacity.

[45:30] Liam: logging: how granular are logs? we need per-route, per-request IDs for tracing.
[45:36] Elena: we can include request ids, traces, and export structured logs to ваша cloud storage or SIEM. note: transcription may have typos but logs will be accurate.

[47:00] Priya: any blockers we should flag now?
[47:05] Maya: internal compliance needs a SOC2 addendum and KMS key ownership doc.
[47:12] Samir: we'll share the security pack and SOC2 report; for KMS we'll outline how to configure customer-managed keys.

[48:30] Elena: ok quick recap of next steps — samir send pricing + pilot contract, elena share benchmark plan, maya share logs + eval set, liam confirm network details. reconvene 2025-08-21 for results review.

[49:10] Raj: sounds good.
[49:20] Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with calendar invites for the kickoff.

[51:00] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-attributions and small transcription errors (e.g., token counts said as tens possibly); technical numbers verified against customer's CSV will be authoritative.
